scope: Known owned-client pause/recovery on accepted r1; original CAMSS diagnostic remains unresolved
pause_target: Only the pidfd-pinned cam primary process and its threads, not the system or unrelated processes
stop_acknowledgement_scope: The as-tested helper checks the primary task state only. It did not independently verify every live thread or the kernel group-stop wait notification; all-thread acknowledgement requires a stronger follow-up.
cleanup_scope: Verified private child session/process group for bounded interrupt/kill/reap; pinned primary fallback on resume/identity failure
interpretation: The client and capture recover from these pauses. Paused cases have one approximately200ms completion gap; controls stay near33.3ms. This experiment does not reproduce either the old diagnostic or the approximately1s file-output gaps.
timing_scope: Driver buffer-completion timestamps, not a sensor frame counter. First new completion after resume excludes buffers already completed during the stop; it is not first application-dequeue latency.
next_diagnostic: An owned trace instance using existing vb2 queue/done tracepoints can measure queued/driver-owned buffers without a new kernel. Preserve globals and remove the owned instance; private raw trace may contain kernel pointers and must not be published. Match the original front/rear binned/full switching sequence when investigating its warning.
source_context: These historical helper hashes refer to the pinned tested commit. Current pause-queue-test.py has the stronger full-thread group-stop follow-up documented separately.
